text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: auth.service.high_401_rate triggered for prod (us-west-2). 401s up ~10x since 10:03 UTC. Sample log shows same session cookie string appearing across multiple edge backends and regions. Suspected proxy log duplication or session-echo.

mike: @anya oncall? grabbing traces and starting triage. pinging infra to isolate offending proxy.

anya: oncall sec here. I see replicated session IDs in our trace aggregator. Suspect edge-proxy-4 and edge-proxy-7. Can someone confirm which proxy shipped those logs to S3?

lisa: checking logshipper. Running: `kubectl -n infra exec -it logshipper-0 -- /bin/sh -c "grep -R \"session=\" /var/log/edge-proxy/* | head -n 50"`

lisa: grep output: multiple entries from edge-proxy-4 and edge-proxy-7 showing same session tokens but different backend target IPs.

harry: I've added a temporary iptables DROP rule on edge-proxy-4 for 52.45.12.0/24 (suspicious source). Also pushed a WAF rule to block UA pattern `curl/7.*(bot|scrape)` to staging edge. :white_check_mark:

anya: Good. We should rotate the session-sync service token (svc-session-sync) and invalidate KV caches for session namespace. mike, can you rotate secret and deploy new token?

mike: Running rotation now: `aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id prod/svc-session-sync`

mike: Rotation succeeded. Bumping new token to canary fleet (10%) then global if healthy.

cust-success: FYI — seeing a spike of 401s for a handful of orgs on us-west. Some users report being logged out. Any ETA?

lisa: Impact: ~4% of login flows returned 401s in last 12m for tenants in us-west. No data exfil confirmed yet; logs show truncated headers only.

anya: I'm searching S3 archive for any uploaded logs that contain session tokens. Command: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs-prod/edge/us-west/2026-03-17/ shard.log - | grep -E "session=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"`

anya: Found one archived shard (s3://redwood-logs-prod/edge/us-west/2026-03-17/edge-shard-1024.log.gz) that contains session tokens and partial headers. Marking shard for quarantine and retention hold.

mike: Quarantining: `aws s3api put-object-tagging --bucket redwood-logs-prod --key edge/us-west/2026-03-17/edge-shard-1024.log.gz --tagging 'TagSet=[{Key=quarantine,Value=true}]'`

mike: Added lifecycle hold, copied snapshot to internal-sec bucket for forensics.

legal: looped in Legal. Preserve all evidence and DO NOT DELETE. If PII or customer tokens present, we may need to follow notification paths. Please add evidence links to the incident ticket.

anya: Creating incident ticket (sec-2026-03-17-echo) with evidence snapshot + checklist. Immediate mitigation checklist: block suspicious IP ranges, rotate svc tokens, quarantine logs, invalidate session KV prefix, enable WAF rule, start customer impact review.

lisa: Invalidating KV cache: `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/kv/invalidate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"prefix":"session:"}'` -> success. Also nuked in-memory session caches on canary nodes.

mike: Monitoring metrics: 401 rate trending down after ip block + token rotation. Will keep canary at 10% for 20m then roll.

cust-success: Preparing customer comms draft — low impact subset affected, recommend message: "Intermittent auth failures observed; we rotated session tokens and are investigating logs. No confirmed data exposure at this time."

anya: Forensics: we saw one archived log file with session tokens. It appears the logshipper duplicated payloads across region shards due to a buffer flush bug in edge-proxy-7. Root cause candidate: logshipper retry on partial write produced duplicate entries.

harry: Patching logshipper to dedupe flushes and bumping to v1.3.7. Rolling to staging now.

legal: keep me posted on confirmed PII. Dont escalate to customers until triage complete and CS approves wording.

mike: Handoff plan: I'll monitor for 30m then hand to night SRE @harry if stable. If 401s rise again, re-open page.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated -> P2 at 10:48 UTC. Runbook attached: auth-echo-v1. Link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/auth-echo-v1

anya: Action items tracked in ticket. Owner: @anya. Next steps: postmortem, timeline, remediation (logshipper dedupe fix), improve canary detection for duplicate session IDs, and extend log retention for forensics.

mike: Thanks team — great coordination. Will file postmortem stub and tag security + infra. :white_check_mark:

(lots of :thumbsup: reactions)
